input:
In today's highly competitive food processing industry, energy efficiency has become an increasingly crucial consideration for plant operators who are looking to reduce costs while also enhancing their sustainability credentials. This summary takes a closer look at an exciting opportunity involving a heat-recovery retrofit at a food plant, an opportunity that could potentially deliver some meaningful savings going forward.

The food plant in question currently uses some 2583 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration alone. According to figures supplied by the equipment vendor, the proposed retrofit is projected to save approximately 12% of that use, which translates into a derived saving of around 310 MWh per year at the vendor figure. The capital cost of the retrofit comes in at $351k. Based on an electricity price of $0.13 per kWh, the derived annual saving works out to roughly $40k, and the derived simple payback is approximately 8.8 years. It is worth noting, however, that the saving figure is a vendor projection and has not been measured at this plant, and refrigeration load in the summer peak month has not been modelled, which means that the real picture may well prove to be somewhat more nuanced than the headline numbers initially suggest. The $351k of capital, in other words, buys a projected $40k per year, and decision-makers will need to weigh that particular trade-off very carefully. Against this backdrop, it is recommended that a metered trial be carried out on one of the three refrigeration lines before any capital decision is taken, with the plant engineer owning the trial and overseeing its implementation.
target:
Recommendation: run a metered trial of heat recovery on one of the three refrigeration lines before any capital decision; the plant engineer owns the trial. The case for the retrofit rests on a vendor projection, and no saving has been measured at this plant.

The food plant uses 2583 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration. The vendor projects a saving of 12% of that use, a derived saving of 310 MWh per year. At an electricity price of $0.13 per kWh, the derived annual saving is $40k, set against a capital cost of $351k, and the derived simple payback is 8.8 years. The trade-off stands in one line: $351k of capital buys a projected $40k per year, at a payback of close to nine years, on a figure the plant has not verified.

Two limits bound the projection. The saving figure is a vendor projection and was not measured at this plant, so it carries the vendor's test conditions rather than this plant's duty. Refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled, so the annual figure may misstate the saving in the months when refrigeration demand is highest. A metered trial on one line closes both before the capital is committed: metering before and after the retrofit gives a measured saving on duty, and a trial that runs through the peak month gives the load shape the projection lacks. The capital decision is taken on the trial result.
